mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 2% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: Equity market remains resilient with SPX returns > 0 over the 20-day horizon following the INDPRO shock, indicating companies are adapting quickly or the shock is transient.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, with the 3-month change exceeding 0.5 percentage points, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSAFS) and consumer confidence surge during the signal period, indicating the labor market weakness is not translating to consumer spending pullback.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Equity market remains resilient with SPX returns > 0 over the 20-day horizon despite the high FEDFUNDS level, indicating the market is looking through the tightening to a soft landing.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise by more than 5% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals a strong consumer demand environment that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence and retail sales (RSAFS) decline sharply during the signal period, indicating the positive HOUST/UNRATE signal is not translating to actual consumer demand.

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM manufacturing index (INDPRO) is above 55 and the CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) is rising by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals a high-inflation regime that will erode corporate profit margins and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Equity market remains resilient with SPX returns > 0 over the 20-day horizon despite the high inflation signal, indicating the market is looking through the inflation to a soft landing.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is rising by more than 200,000 jobs per month, it signals a tight labor market that will boost wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Wage growth (from the Employment Cost Index) fails to accelerate during the signal period, indicating the tight labor market is not translating to higher consumer spending power.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the 2-year Treasury yield is above the 10-year yield (yield curve inversion), it signals a looming recession that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Leading economic indicators (e.g., PMI, consumer confidence) remain strong during the signal period, indicating the yield curve inversion is not signaling an imminent recession.
